title: Tanzanian Beef Peanut Stew
community: Popular in central and western Tanzania
author: Mama Salima
desc: Mchuzi wa Nyama na Karanga — Tanzanian beef and peanut stew. Tender beef simmered in a rich sauce of ground peanuts, tomatoes, and spices. A thick, nourishing, deeply satisfying stew from central Tanzania — the peanut sauce provides protein and richness that transforms the dish.
longDesc: Peanut stew is one of central Tanzania's most beloved dishes — the ground peanuts create a sauce of extraordinary richness and depth that coats the beef perfectly. It is a dish of warmth, nourishment, and deep satisfaction.
ingredients: 1 cup raw peanuts — roasted and ground (or 4 tbsp peanut butter)
steps: Roast peanuts in a dry pan until golden. Cool and grind coarsely.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, spices.
Return beef. Add water. Simmer covered 40 minutes.
Mix ground peanuts with ½ cup warm water to a paste. Add to pot.
Simmer 15—20 more minutes until sauce is thick and richly flavoured.
chefTips: Freshly roasted and ground peanuts are vastly better than commercial peanut butter.
Mix peanut paste with warm water first — prevents lumping.
The peanut sauce should be thick and coating.
commonMistakes: Adding dry ground peanuts directly — lumps.
Commercial peanut butter substituted without adjusting salt.
cookingScience: Ground peanuts contain protein and fat that emulsify into the stew liquid during cooking, creating a naturally thick, rich sauce without the need for flour or starch. The peanut fat carries the spice flavours throughout the sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Peanuts are a nitrogen-fixing legume — growing them improves soil fertility.
healthBenefits: Complete protein from beef and peanuts.
culturalNote: Beef peanut stew represents the culinary traditions of Tanzania's interior — where groundnuts have been grown and cooked with for centuries, long before the coast's coconut influence reached inland.
